pass_a_gloss: [...] clearly, naming them a multitude of nations. And they came upon the countries, that is, the cities of Judaea, like much water and as rushed down by force, and making uproars, and all but like the sea surging over those who resisted. And he calls them in these [words] back of many nations, because many nations were pursued by them. And the pursuers run in every way and wholly at the back of those fleeing. Then what after this? He will drive him off, he says, that is, he will send him back, and will pursue him far, like the fine dust of chaff of winnowers before the wind, and like dust of a wheel which a storm carries. For what is so easily blown away as dust from a wheel and a threshing floor, when a violent wind sweeps down? And that Sennacherib went off a fugitive the God of all will confirm, saying to him through the voice of Isaiah: And I will put a muzzle into your nose, and a bridle into your lips, and I will turn you back on the road by which you came. [Lemma, Isaiah 17:14:] Toward evening there will be mourning before morning, and it will not be. This is the portion of those who plundered you, and inheritance of those who inherited you. I said before that Rabshakeh, having set the fighting force around Jerusalem, and having threatened to take it before long, perished with the whole army before dawn and day. There will be mourning then, he says, toward evening, those in Jerusalem surely expecting that the attack of the war would be in the morning, but it ceased before dawn. Because of this he says: There will be mourning toward evening; but it will not be before morning, that is, the tear will cease and come to an end; and together with the fears of suffering it will go away, God helping and having destroyed beyond expectation the phalanxes of the enemies, and besides having driven the leader out of the land of the Jews. This the blessed David also explains, saying: At evening weeping will lodge, and toward morning gladness. But this, he says, is the lot; and this the portion of those who plundered you and snatched you as their own lot. He reproaches through these things those from Israel, that they themselves did the things through which it was likely the nation would perish root and all, but he again pities, and punishes with death those who plunder the people allotted to him. For when, it says, the Most High was dividing nations, as he scattered sons of Adam, he set boundaries of nations according to the number of angels of God; and his people Jacob became portion of the Lord, measured line of his inheritance Israel. But besides these things look finely at that too, and as from the things that happened historically come into the innermost thoughts. Whenever the wicked and opposing powers, pouring down upon the soul like violent water, either by things from outside [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: …plainly, calling them a multitude of nations. They came upon the lands, that is, the cities of Judea, like a great flood of water rushing down with violence and raising a roar, all but sweeping over those who resisted like the waves of the sea.
Here he calls them “the back of many nations” (Isaiah 17:12), because many nations were pursued by them; and pursuers always and everywhere run at the backs of those who flee.

Then what follows? “He will drive him off,” he says, that is, he will send him back, “and pursue him far away, like the fine chaff of winnowers before the wind, and like the dust of a wheel which a storm carries” (Isaiah 17:13). For what is so easily scattered as dust from a wheel and a threshing floor when a fierce wind sweeps down on it?

That Sennacherib went off a fugitive, the God of all will confirm when he says to him through the voice of Isaiah: “I will put a muzzle in your nose and a bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came” (Isaiah 37:29).
“Toward evening there will be mourning; before morning it will be no more. This is the portion of those who plundered you, and the inheritance of those who inherited you” (Isaiah 17:14).

I said earlier that Rabshakeh surrounded Jerusalem with his fighting force and threatened to take it before long, but perished with his whole army before dawn and daylight. So there will be mourning toward evening, he says, since those in Jerusalem no doubt expected the assault of the war to come in the morning; but it ended before dawn.

That is why he says: There will be mourning toward evening, but before morning it will be no more. That is, the weeping will stop and come to an end, and it will vanish together with the fear of suffering, since God comes to their help, destroys the enemy's ranks beyond all expectation, and drives their leader out of the land of the Jews besides.
The blessed David also explains this when he says: “At evening weeping will stay the night, and at morning there will be gladness” (Psalm 30:5).

But this, he says, is the lot, this the portion of those who plundered you and seized you as their own inheritance. By these words he reproaches the people of Israel: they themselves had done the things for which the nation might well have perished utterly, yet he takes pity on them once more and punishes with death those who plunder the people allotted to him.

For, it says, “when the Most High divided the nations, when he scattered the sons of Adam, he set the boundaries of the nations according to the number of the angels of God; and his people Jacob became the Lord's portion, Israel the measured lot of his inheritance” (Deuteronomy 32:8–9).

But besides this, consider this point carefully with me, and pass, as it were, from the events of history to the inmost meanings. When the wicked and hostile powers, pouring over the soul like violent water, either by trials from without…

choices.term: μό- νον δὲ οὐχὶ θαλάσσης δίκην
choices.english: all but sweeping over those who resisted like the waves of the sea
choices.why: μόνον οὐχί means 'all but', not 'but not'; the enemy armies are likened to the sea.
Septuagint Isaiah 17:12 wording; Cyril explains it from pursuers running at the backs of the fleeing.
The quotation is Isaiah 37:29, God's word to Sennacherib.
αὐλίζομαι is to lodge for the night (Psalm 30:5).

choices.english: takes pity on them once more
choices.why: God pities Israel and punishes the plunderers; the subject is God.
